title: NP certificates of bounded length
statement: A language $L$ over the binary alphabet belongs to $\mathsf{NP}$ if and only if there are natural numbers $C,c$ and a language $V\in\mathsf{P}$ such that, for every binary string $x$, $x\in L$ exactly when there is a binary string $u$ with $|u|\le C(|x|+1)^c$ for which $\langle x,u\rangle\in V$. Here $\langle x,u\rangle$ is formed by doubling each bit of $x$, appending the separator $01$, and then appending $u$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language over the binary alphabet
replaced:
For a language $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$, the following are equivalent:
(i) $L \in \mathsf{NP}$, i.e.\ there are $C', c' \in \mathbb{N}$ and a language
$V' \in \mathsf{P}$ such that for every binary string $x$, $x \in L$ if and only if
some $u$ with $|u| = C'(|x|+1)^{c'}$ has $xu \in V'$;
(ii) there are $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ and a language $V \in \mathsf{P}$ such that
for every binary string $x$, $x \in L$ if and only if some binary string $u$ with
$|u| \le C(|x|+1)^c$ has $\langle x, u\rangle \in V$, where
$\langle x, u\rangle$ is the self-delimiting pair encoding consisting of $x$ with
every bit doubled, then the separator $01$, then $u$ verbatim.
